claims.title: Peopling of the river basins
claims.summary: Indigenous peoples occupy the basins of the Parana and Paraguay rivers over many millennia, with Guarani-speaking farming and forest peoples coming to predominate in the historic era.

sources.label: Paraguay: A Country Study
sources.publisher: Library of Congress, Federal Research Division

claims.title: Founding of Asuncion
claims.summary: Spaniards complete a stockade on the Paraguay River on the feast of the Assumption, founding Asuncion, the 'mother of cities' from which much of the south was settled.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1537-founding-of-asuncion, claim TL:PRY:event:1537:founding-of-asuncion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Asuncion becomes the Spanish base
claims.summary: After the first Buenos Aires is abandoned, its survivors flee to Asuncion, which becomes the headquarters of Spanish colonial activity in eastern South America.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1541-asuncion-becomes-the-spanish-base, claim TL:PRY:event:1541:asuncion-becomes-the-spanish-base, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Jesuit reducciones
claims.summary: The Jesuits gather up to 150,000 Guarani into some thirty mission towns in the Parana and Uruguay basins, blending Indigenous labour with Christian instruction and Baroque art.

sources.label: Jesuit Missions of La Santisima Trinidad de Parana and Jesus de Tavarangue

claims.title: Treaty of Madrid and the Guarani War
claims.summary: A planned transfer of seven mission towns to Portugal provokes Guarani resistance and a Spanish-Portuguese campaign, hardening official hostility to the Jesuits.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1750-treaty-of-madrid-and-the-guarani-war, claim TL:PRY:event:1750:treaty-of-madrid-and-the-guarani-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Expulsion of the Jesuits
claims.summary: Charles III expels the Jesuits from Spanish America; the Guarani missions are abandoned and fall into ruin, their populations scattered.

sources.label: Jesuit Missions of La Santisima Trinidad de Parana and Jesus de Tavarangue

claims.title: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
claims.summary: The new viceroyalty centred on Buenos Aires makes Asuncion and Paraguay dependent on the river port, feeding Paraguayan resentment of its decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1776-viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata, claim TL:PRY:event:1776:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from Spain
claims.summary: Paraguayan officers depose the Spanish governor at Asuncion without bloodshed, ending colonial rule; a republic is proclaimed in 1813.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1811-independence-from-spain, claim TL:PRY:event:1811:independence-from-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The dictatorship of Dr Francia
claims.summary: Jose Gaspar Rodriguez de Francia rules as Supreme Dictator, sealing Paraguay off from the world in near-total isolation until his death.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1814-the-dictatorship-of-dr-francia, claim TL:PRY:event:1814:the-dictatorship-of-dr-francia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Carlos Antonio Lopez modernises Paraguay
claims.summary: Ending Francia's isolation, Carlos Antonio Lopez opens the country, signs commercial treaties, and builds railways, foundries and schools while enlarging the army.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1841-carlos-antonio-lopez-modernises-paraguay, claim TL:PRY:event:1841:carlos-antonio-lopez-modernises-paraguay, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Francisco Solano Lopez takes power
claims.summary: On his father's death, Francisco Solano Lopez becomes leader, inheriting a large army and ambitions that would soon plunge Paraguay into war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1862-francisco-solano-lopez-takes-power, claim TL:PRY:event:1862:francisco-solano-lopez-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Paraguay invades Mato Grosso
claims.summary: Francisco Solano Lopez opens hostilities by invading the Brazilian province of Mato Grosso, the first move in a war that would soon include Argentina and Uruguay.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1864-paraguay-invades-mato-grosso, claim TL:PRY:event:1864:paraguay-invades-mato-grosso, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of the Triple Alliance
claims.summary: Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay sign a secret alliance against Paraguay, committing to wage war until the fall of Lopez.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1865-treaty-of-the-triple-alliance, claim TL:PRY:event:1865:treaty-of-the-triple-alliance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Battle of Tuyuti
claims.summary: The allies inflict a heavy defeat on Paraguay at Tuyuti, one of the largest battles of the war, beginning the slow destruction of Lopez's army.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1866-battle-of-tuyuti, claim TL:PRY:event:1866:battle-of-tuyuti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Lopez at Cerro Cora
claims.summary: Brazilian troops kill Francisco Solano Lopez at Cerro Cora, ending the war; Paraguay has lost territory and a vast, disputed share of its population (figures are estimates).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1870-death-of-lopez-at-cerro-cora, claim TL:PRY:event:1870:death-of-lopez-at-cerro-cora, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rebuilding and the party system
claims.summary: Paraguay slowly rebuilds after the war as foreign capital returns and land is sold off; the Colorado and Liberal parties emerge to dominate national politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1870-rebuilding-and-the-party-system, claim TL:PRY:event:1870:rebuilding-and-the-party-system, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Chaco War
claims.summary: Paraguay and Bolivia fight a costly war over the Gran Chaco; about 100,000 men die before a 1935 truce, with most of the region awarded to Paraguay by the 1938 treaty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1932-the-chaco-war, claim TL:PRY:event:1932:the-chaco-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Paraguayan Civil War
claims.summary: A brief, bloody civil war ends in victory for the Colorado Party, entrenching one-party dominance and clearing the path to authoritarian rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1947-paraguayan-civil-war, claim TL:PRY:event:1947:paraguayan-civil-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Stroessner seizes power
claims.summary: General Alfredo Stroessner overthrows President Federico Chaves and assumes the presidency, beginning a thirty-five-year dictatorship under the Colorado Party.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1954-stroessner-seizes-power, claim TL:PRY:event:1954:stroessner-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Itaipu dam begins generating
claims.summary: The binational Itaipu hydroelectric dam on the Parana, built with Brazil under a 1973 treaty, starts producing power, transforming Paraguay's economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1984-itaipu-dam-begins-generating, claim TL:PRY:event:1984:itaipu-dam-begins-generating, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Overthrow of Stroessner
claims.summary: General Andres Rodriguez ousts Stroessner in a coup and wins elections later that year, opening Paraguay's transition to democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1989-overthrow-of-stroessner, claim TL:PRY:event:1989:overthrow-of-stroessner, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: New democratic constitution
claims.summary: A Constituent Assembly enacts a constitution establishing a presidential republic and making Guarani co-official with Spanish.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-1992-new-democratic-constitution, claim TL:PRY:event:1992:new-democratic-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First opposition victory
claims.summary: Former bishop Fernando Lugo wins the presidency, ending more than sixty years of Colorado Party rule in Paraguay's first electoral transfer of power between parties.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Paraguay: From the Guarani world of the great rivers and the Spanish founding of Asuncion to the Jesuit missions, independence in 1811, the isolation of Dr Francia and the Lopez dynasty, the catastrophe of the Triple Alliance war, the Chaco War, the long Stroessner dictatorship, and a democratic, Guarani-speaking republic in the age of Itaipu.", terralore.co/country/PRY/chronicle#ev-2008-first-opposition-victory, claim TL:PRY:event:2008:first-opposition-victory, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
